doc.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Buddy Rich records and what Kay learned from him
summary: Kay recalls getting Bill Reddy to write West Side Story for Rich and says drumming for Buddy taught him to represent Sherrie's band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: They had some outstanding records. I know in college we used to just — we wore out “Channel One Suite.” And all us guys, we’d just listen to that.
Well I got Bill Reddy to write the “West Side Story” for him. I knew Bill from Vegas.

Yeah, absolutely. But I’m fortunate. And then it’s because of him that — whether I could play or not — but I was his drummer, that means I was able to play. But that enabled me to learn, and I’m still learning, because you’re never too old to learn, about how to handle or try to represent Sherrie and our band in the best way possible. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-
